transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we finalize the rollout. While tracing a separate permissions bug yesterday, I found that 23 legacy admin endpoints update permissions without emitting the invalidation event that the new cache depends on. I haven't filed the adapter work yet because I was still confirming which endpoints use that path. The rollout plan must include a binding commitment to build and verify an invalidation adapter for those 23 endpoints before we expand beyond the initial cohort.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share the results from the load rehearsal I ran this morning. Invalidation-queue propagation measured at a 9-minute p95, and the queue stays within its safe operating limit only if the first rollout cohort is capped at 10 percent. Additionally, the authorization cache lifetime must be set to exactly 300 seconds for this rollout. I haven't updated the rollout ticket yet because the rehearsal finished after the change-control review had already begun.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share a finding from a support-case review I completed. All 11 SCIM-managed enterprise accounts use an admin workflow that cannot yet explain delayed permission changes. These accounts must be excluded from the first rollout cohort, and a support playbook must be prepared before they are enabled. I hadn't posted this yet because the cases were being reassigned between support queues.
transcript.speaker: A4

commitments.detail: Build and verify an invalidation adapter for the 23 legacy admin endpoints that update permissions without emitting the invalidation event, before expanding beyond the initial 10% rollout cohort.
Update the rollout ticket with the load rehearsal results, including the 9-minute p95 propagation finding and the 10% cohort cap requirement.
Monitor invalidation-queue depth and p95 propagation during the initial cohort rollout; halt expansion if queue exceeds safe operating limits.
Prepare a support playbook for delayed permission changes before SCIM-managed enterprise accounts are enabled in any future cohort.
Maintain a revocation kill switch enabled for the rollout, allowing immediate rollback if authorization-cache issues surface in production.
